headline: Lahad Datu at 13: no kidnappings since 2020, but ESSCOM's island base stalled at 41%
context: The 2013 Lahad Datu incursion left at least 68 intruders and 10 security personnel dead. ESSCOM, set up on 1 April 2013, had recorded no kidnappings since 2020 by March 2025. Its Pulau Mabul base was 41% complete in October 2025, at 54% over budget.

changes.summary: Correction: Earlier editions said ESSCOM was set up by executive directive and has no Act of Parliament, and that its sea curfew had run for nearly 12 years; we could not confirm either and have removed both. We also corrected Sabah's poverty rate to 19.7%, added the 10 security personnel killed in 2013, and removed an unsourced claim about named communities.

cards.big: ESSCOM marks 13 years: zero kidnappings since 2020, but its Pulau Mabul forward base was only 41% complete in October 2025
cards.sub: The 2013 Lahad Datu incursion left at least 68 intruders and 10 security personnel dead. ESSCOM was set up on 1 April 2013.

cards.big: 59 kidnapping attempts foiled and zero cases since January 2020, though decline also reflects Philippine ops against Abu Sayyaf and COVID border closures
cards.sub: Pulau Mabul forward base only 41% complete after a decade, costs rose from RM52.81M to RM81.51M after contractor failure

cards.big: Eastern Sabah's sea curfew has run on renewals. Police extended it for the 215th time in July 2023, nine years after it began.
cards.sub: The curfew was first imposed on 16 July 2014, under Section 31(4) of the Police Act 1967.

cards.big: The security zone covers 1,400 km of coastline in a state with 1.04 million non-citizens and Malaysia's highest poverty rate
cards.sub: Sabah's poverty rate was 19.7% in 2022, against 6.2% nationally, the Statistics Department found.

cards.big: ESSCOM works. Its foundations do not: a base 41% built after a decade, and a sea curfew renewed 215 times by 2023.
ESSCOM is a genuine security success on fragile foundations. Renewing a curfew 215 times makes a habit, not a plan.
